hook_text: Some villages are circles. Some are straight lines. Some literally write the letter T on the landscape. None of it is random.
clip_script: Round: the traditional homestead layout — dwellings standing in a ring with the cattle kraal at the centre. The circle wraps around what is precious. Linear: recall any stretch of rural road where every single building faces the tar — the village has taken the shape of the thing it clings to: beads on a string, because everyone wants a front door on the route. Where a side road dead-ends against a main road, buildings gather along both arms and the village writes a letter T. Where two roads cross, the village writes an X. The cause is the same for both: a junction is where traffic slows, stops and turns — and wherever travellers pause, someone sells to them. The junction is a magnet; the shape is just the iron filings around it.
visual_style: Satellite-style zooms: a ring village around a kraal, a ribbon village hugging a road, then a T and an X materialising at junctions, with shape outlines glowing over the rooftops.
pacing: Four quick zoom reveals, one beat per shape, magnet line as the final punch.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to read any village's shape — and its reason — on sight.
